I will still do wheat and maize on the full 5 mu, same as before. On my land, changing the cropping pattern is risky, and with a well I can hold yield steady if the weather is not too bad. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too complicated. I start from what worked last year, then I look at what the better farmers around me are doing. For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because the stand is more even and the ears fill better. I will not cut fertilizer too hard. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose grain, that loss is bigger than the fertilizer money. So I will keep wheat nitrogen a bit stronger, with phosphorus put in early and some potassium too. I have irrigation, so I will water wheat about 3 times if the season is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed. Around here, people have seen hybrid maize give more stable yield, so I will follow that. Maize eats fertilizer too, especially nitrogen, and if rain comes unevenly, I can still use the well to carry it through. I will keep pesticide use to what is needed, usually 2 times for each crop if insects or disease show up. On 5 mu, I still think carefully about money, but I would rather spend a bit more and protect the harvest than hold back and regret it later.
